text:
Predicates:
Cost(x, y) ::: It costs x US dollars to take the GRE test.
FinancialAid(x, y) ::: ETS provides financial aid to GRE applicants who prove y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
SingleParent(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
OutOfWork(x, y) ::: x has been out of work for more than y.
Premises:
Cost(205, GRE) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (FinancialAid(x, EconomicHardship(x))) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
∀x (EconomicHardship(x) ↔ (TooLittleMoney(x) ∨ TooFewResources(x))) ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
SingleParent(tom) ∧ OutOfWork(dad, 1 year) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family. His dad has been out of work for more than a year.
Conclusion:
FinancialAid(tom, EconomicHardship(tom)) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
